intent: The restore ceremony's failure sentences stop being body text and take the danger role every other ceremony wears.
rationale: The three strategy lifecycle ceremonies render their failure sentences as bare `role="alert" className="text-sm"` — body text, distinguishable from ordinary prose only by a screen reader. DT-0004 decided what a failed attempt looks like (danger.subtle on danger.default, the state named as well as tinted) and every ceremony built or swept since wears it; these three predate the sweep and were surveyed only after it. The sentences here are the platform's own words about why a strategy could not be retired, restored or copied — what the operator came to read — and they currently carry less weight than the paragraph explaining what a blank fork name does. The carried-problem banner is not restyled: it is CarriedProblem's and already correct. Where both are present the two share the danger role deliberately, because they are the same kind of fact — one about the attempt that bounced here, one about the read that failed on arrival — and the outcome requirement exists for exactly the case where both are true.

acceptance: The restore page's unreadable-branch reason renders on color.danger.subtle with a 1px color.danger.default border, and keeps role=alert
WhyNotLoaded's reassurance renders immediately after that block, verbatim and outside the danger tint — a sentence whose whole job is 'your work is not gone' must not itself be dressed as a failure
Any refused-describe reason on this page renders in the same treatment
A no-such-strategy branch stays plain prose — it is an answer, not a failure
The carried-problem banner is unchanged; where both render, both are visible
Zero copy changes anywhere on the page
No raw color, spacing, or size literal is introduced

Corrected 2026-08-12, after implementation: this ticket first said the reassurance renders *inside* the danger block. It does not, and should not — it renders immediately after it. Caught by the post-round re-survey reading the code against the acceptance, which is what that pass is for. The criterion was wrong, not the implementation.
